## Rail-served opening serves bulk, project cargo 

 Stuart Chirls 

· Wednesday, September 09, 2026 

 Foundation 3 is shown under construction in August 2026. (Photo: Colonial Terminals) 

Colonial Terminals has opened Foundation 3, a new 25-acre multimodal breakbulk facility on the Savannah River, expanding capacity and connectivity for bulk and project cargo moving through the Port of Savannah region.

The terminal, designed for 24-hour operations, adds direct vessel access via an 810-foot heavy-capacity dock, onsite rail yard with more than 14,000 feet of track, terminal-operated switching, and rail-served warehouse access. It connects to Class I rail service through Norfolk Southern and offers highway access via interstates 16 and 95, for seamless transfers across ship, rail, truck, and warehouse operations. 

Foundation 3 includes two warehouses totaling 130,000 square feet, including a newly renovated dockside site, and a 75,000-square-foot concrete outdoor storage area, with adjacent acreage reserved for future expansion.

## LTL carrier’s North American terminal count reaches 300 

 Todd Maiden 

· Thursday, October 01, 2026 

 XPO expanded its North American footprint to 300 terminals following the addition of new service centers in Missouri and Arizona. (Photo: Jim Allen/FreightWaves) 

Less-than-truckload carrier XPO announced Thursday that it has added new locations in Arizona and Missouri, increasing its terminal count to 300 across North America.

A new 51,000-square-foot facility in Mesa, Arizona has 86 dock doors and over 100 employees. The terminal gives XPO (NYSE: XPO) needed capacity to serve the Phoenix market, where it already operates a freight assembly center. The region is experiencing an increase in demand given recent industrial investments and growing cross-border trade with Mexico.

A 13,000-square-foot terminal in Cameron, Missouri (approximately 50 miles north of Kansas City) has 32 dock doors and over 30 employees. It sits near the intersection of I-35 and U.S. 36, serving both north-south and east-west freight corridors.

# PTL Expands Transload Network to Include Elizabeth, New Jersey

Jul 15 1 min read

Effective June 28, Precision Terminal Logistics has been awarded operations of the Norfolk Southern Thoroughbred Bulk Transload (NS TBT) facility in Elizabeth, New Jersey.

The Elizabeth facility offers significant capacity with 160 rail spots, warehouse space, ground storage, and a certified truck scale. Ideally located within 10 miles of I-95, Newark Liberty International Airport, the New York Container Terminal, and NS-served ports in the NY/NJ area, it is well positioned to serve a broad range of customers. The site can accommodate aggregates, food-grade materials, liquids, lumber, steel, and other commodities.

“This new location builds directly on our recent opening in Pottstown, Pennsylvania, creating strong connectivity along the Eastern Seaboard,” said David Kearney, CEO of Precision Terminal Logistics. “Each new facility expands the connections we can make for our clients.”

results.author: PTL
results.text:
PTL Adds Syracuse, NY, CSX TRANSFLO Facility to Transload Network

# PTL Adds Syracuse, NY, CSX TRANSFLO Facility to Transload Network

Aug 5 1 min read

The Syracuse CSX TRANSFLO facility is the newest addition to the Precision Terminal Logistics network, effective July 1. PTL now operates 14 TRANSFLO terminals across the country. 

The Syracuse location offers 55 railcar spots and sits near the intersection of I-690 and I-481 for convenient highway access. It is a multi-commodity facility capable of handling a variety of products, including dry bulk, food-grade, and liquid products. The facility also offers heating to ensure your freight is safe in winter conditions.

PTL is proud to maintain its relationship with CSX TRANSFLO and looks forward to providing operational services.

“Our expansion over the last month has been fast-paced but very intentional — we’ve been preparing for these opportunities for some time,” said Ray Nixon, President and COO of Precision Terminal Logistics. “Our team is energized and ready to elevate operations at both sites.”

The new 315,000-square-foot facility replaces G10's former Twin Lakes location and more than doubles the company's Midwest warehouse capacity. Positioned along the Chicago–Milwaukee freight corridor, the site supports large-scale order fulfillment and regional inventory distribution as part of G10's broader logistics network.
